review_comments.body: I'd build the activity from the pre-update read and the request instead of the read after the update. That read goes to the replica, so with replica lag a full edit can log the old labels.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Make the expected label comparison independent of array order.** `lastActivityMatches` uses `assert.JSONEq`, which requires array elements in the same order. The expectation at lines 330-331 lists `lbl1` before `lbl2`. The stored-label read behind this activity, `getVPPAppLabels`, has no `ORDER BY`. Its row order can therefore vary, so the activity can contain `[lbl2, lbl1]` and fail this assertion even when it contains the correct labels. Check label membership without depending on array order. Options include comparing the labels array separately with an order-insensitive assertion, or normalizing both sides before comparing.

Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** Issue `#58486` requires that the edited App Store app activity show the version's labels and configuration after an API edit, whatever fields the request includes. The current head changes the data source. Per the whole-PR change summary for ee/server/service/vpp.go, UpdateAppStoreApp builds activity labels from the pre-update version and overlays request labels only when labels are supplied. Activity configuration uses the request value when present, otherwise the stored configuration, with iOS/iPadOS plist bytes still wrapped as a JSON string. For the reported name-only edit, the stored labels and configuration are used, which matches the issue's expected behavior. Automated coverage is TestUpdateAppStoreAppActivityKeepsStoredSettings in ee/server/service/vpp_test.go. It simulates a lagging re-read and asserts the stored labels and configuration. TestSoftwareTitleDisplayNames is updated to expect labels in the activity. Limitation: the vpp.go diff blob was unavailable and the vpp.go file read was truncated before UpdateAppStoreApp. The code behavior therefore rests on the change summary and PR description, not on a direct read of the changed lines. The previous PASS relied on the earlier re-read approach and is superseded by this new source-selection rule.

Thanks for the review. Pushed a follow-up commit:

- The activity's labels and configuration are now built from the pre-update read and the request (request value when given, stored value from the pre-update read otherwise), not from the post-update read, so replica lag can't log the old labels. The response still uses the re-read, as before.
- `TestSoftwareTitleDisplayNames`: the display-name edit activity now carries the app's labels, so the expected activity includes `labels_include_any`. The unit test now simulates a lagging re-read (no labels/config) and still expects the stored values.
- Updated the PR description to follow the PR template.

This update was prepared with AI assistance (Claude) and submitted by the account owner.
